description: The rule's name. Rows sharing a rule_id are ANDed into one rule; different rule_ids are ORed, so a crossing is a human-made barrier where any rule matches. Each crossing's matching rule_ids are written, sorted and joined with ';', to crossings.barrier_rule_id. Row order means nothing.

The crossing sources the row applies to: '*', or any of PSCIS, CABD, MODELLED_CROSSINGS. A row matches no crossing outside them, which is how a scenario replaces the province's result for assessed crossings and keeps the modelled type for the rest.

Where the row's column is read: crossings (the crossing row itself) or pscis_assessment (whse_fish.pscis_assessment_svw, joined on stream_crossing_id for a PSCIS crossing; its derived slope_length is culvert_slope times length_or_width). Any other value is refused.
The column compared. Refused when the source does not carry it.
One of in, =, >, >=, <, <=, is_null, not_null. A NULL value matches only is_null.
The value compared, typed by the column (a number for a numeric column) and quoted through DBI; for in, a ';'-separated list.
Which species the rule applies to. Only '*' is accepted until a rule can block a species; anything else is refused at load.
What a match means. Only 'barrier' (a human-made barrier: barrier-below marks, mapping codes and per-crossing totals, never access) is accepted; anything else is refused at load.
When the row was added or last changed.
Where the rule comes from: an assessment protocol, a study, or an issue.
